title: ISR Design
description: Writes interrupt service routines that do the minimum - acknowledge, capture, defer the rest - keeping interrupt context short. Good ISRs are measured in microseconds; everything else belongs in deferred work.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Priority Levels
description: Assigns each interrupt a priority so urgent events preempt less urgent ones deterministically. Thoughtful priority assignment is the core design act of a real-time system.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Nested Interrupts
description: Allows higher-priority interrupts to preempt lower-priority handlers, keeping critical events responsive even during long ISRs. Nesting needs careful stack sizing since preemption depth multiplies stack use.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Latency Budgets
description: Budgets the total time from hardware event to handler response, allocating slices to hardware, ISR, and deferred work. Budgets make latency a contract: measured, tested, and guaranteed.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Deferred Work
description: Pushes heavy processing out of interrupt context into tasklets, workqueues, or threads that run later. Deferred work keeps ISRs short while still handling complex events completely.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Interrupt Affinity
description: Pins interrupts to specific CPU cores so cache-hot handlers stay local and noisy interrupts do not disturb real-time cores. Affinity is essential on multicore real-time systems.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Watchdog Timers
description: Requires software to pet the watchdog regularly; a hung handler or crashed task triggers a reset. Watchdogs are the last line of defense that turns hangs into recoveries.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Deadline Monitoring
description: Timestamps interrupt entry and exit to verify handlers meet their deadlines in production, not just in testing. Monitoring catches the rare deadline misses that testing never reproduces.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Jitter Analysis
description: Measures the variation in interrupt response time, since real-time correctness often depends on consistency more than average speed. Jitter analysis finds the rare outliers that averages hide.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Critical Sections
description: Protects shared data between ISRs and tasks by briefly disabling interrupts or using lock-free structures. Short, well-placed critical sections keep data consistent without wrecking latency.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Lock-Free ISRs
description: Uses lock-free ring buffers and atomics so ISRs never block on locks that a preempted task might hold. Lock-free design eliminates a whole class of deadlock and priority-inversion bugs.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Interrupt Storms
description: Detects when a faulty device fires interrupts thousands of times per second and throttles or disables the source before it wedges the system. Storm protection turns a hardware fault into a logged event instead of a lockup.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Timestamping
description: Captures hardware timestamps at interrupt entry for precise event timing, essential for measurement and control. Accurate timestamps turn interrupts into a time-measurement instrument.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Handler Registration
description: Registers handlers in a vector table with validation that each slot holds a sane address before interrupts are enabled. Validated registration catches the miswired vectors that cause the most confusing crashes.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Worst-Case Analysis
description: Computes worst-case execution time for handlers and the whole interrupt load, proving the system schedulable. WCET analysis replaces hope with math for systems where missing a deadline is not an option.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
